title: T1598.003 — Phishing for Information - Spearphishing Link
subtitle: The animation below plays the whole attack in eight steps.
aria: Animated simulation of spearphishing with a link. An attacker stages a fake login page on a lookalike domain, an employee clicks a link and types credentials, and the SOC contains the access in eight steps.

nodes.label: Attacker
nodes.tip: The threat actor running the credential-harvesting site.

nodes.label: Email
nodes.tip: The message that carries the link. Its headers and links are very useful for responders.

nodes.label: DNS / Proxy
nodes.tip: Your DNS and proxy see every click that leaves the company. Earliest strong signal.

nodes.label: Employee
nodes.tip: The person who clicks. Anyone can click on a busy day.

nodes.label: Fake SSO Page
nodes.tip: A copy of your login page on a lookalike domain. It only collects, never signs in.

nodes.label: IdP / MFA
nodes.tip: Your identity provider. Watch for logins from odd networks right after a campaign.

nodes.label: SOC / Defender
nodes.tip: Your security team. They block domains, kill sessions, and reset passwords.

steps.title: Stage site
steps.caption: The attacker registers a lookalike domain and copies the company login page pixel by pixel.
steps.defender: New domains appear in Certificate Transparency logs within minutes. Watch that feed.

fields.detail: The attacker registers a lookalike domain and copies the company login page pixel by pixel.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Send link
steps.caption: An email asks the employee to 're-verify' access with a link. The story feels routine.
steps.defender: The gateway sees the new domain. Domain age and reputation matter here.

fields.detail: An email asks the employee to 're-verify' access with a link. The story feels routine.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Click
steps.caption: The employee clicks. The request passes your DNS and proxy on the way out.
steps.defender: This is the earliest strong signal: a click to a fresh lookalike domain.

fields.detail: The employee clicks. The request passes your DNS and proxy on the way out.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Fake page
steps.caption: The page looks exactly like the real SSO login. Only the URL is different.
steps.defender: Users read pages, not URLs. Link rewriting and browser isolation help here.

fields.detail: The page looks exactly like the real SSO login. Only the URL is different.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Creds posted
steps.caption: The employee types their username and password. The fake page saves them and shows an error.
steps.defender: No real sign-in appears in your IdP yet. The theft is silent.

fields.detail: The employee types their username and password. The fake page saves them and shows an error.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Access try
steps.caption: The attacker tries the stolen login against the real portal, often within minutes.
steps.defender: IdP logs show a new session from an unfamiliar network or country.

fields.detail: The attacker tries the stolen login against the real portal, often within minutes.

detection.label: Partial signal
detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: MFA push
steps.caption: A real MFA prompt fires. The employee, still expecting the 're-verification', approves it.
steps.defender: A prompt the user did not start is an incident, not noise. Alert on odd MFA bursts.

fields.detail: A real MFA prompt fires. The employee, still expecting the 're-verification', approves it.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: Contain
steps.caption: The SOC blocks the domain, revokes sessions, and forces a password reset.
steps.defender: Speed matters. Revoke before the attacker turns credentials into access.

fields.detail: The SOC blocks the domain, revokes sessions, and forces a password reset.

detection.label: Contained
detection.detail: The activity is contained and the lesson is captured.
